Here’s Your Chance To Buy a Porsche Boxster for Cheap in USA
14 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
If you know your Porsches, and Boxsters in particular, then you are aware of the fact that there is no catch here. But if you don’t, then you will probably be disappointed to find out that this is a first-generation example.
That would make it a 986, which saw the light of day at the Stuttgart factory in Germany between 1996 and 2004, sharing some nuts and bolts with the 996 911, and being essentially a more affordable and less powerful alternative to the 911. And in case you forgot, it features a mid-engine and rear-wheel drive, and was available with three flat-six units back in the day, paired with a manual or an automatic transmissions.
This Porsche Boxster features the stick shift with five forward gears, which is hooked up to a 2.7-liter flat-six engine that was originally good for 217 hp (220 ps/162 kW) and 192 lb-ft (260 Nm) of torque, the ad reveals. The 17-inch alloys, multi-adjustable power seats, a power folding soft-top, and cruise control are some of the things mentioned in the ad as being a partial list of notable equipment when it comes to this 2002 model year open-top sports car.
Photo: Cars&Bids Finished in Seal Gray on top of a Gray interior, which is a very early-2000s look, the Porsche Boxster in question has a clean Florida title, and is currently located in Boca Raton, FL. At the time of cataloging, the odometer read 47,400 miles (76,300 km), and given that it is roughly 25 years old, that’s not bad at all, is it? That translates to just under 1,900 miles (~3,050 km) per year on average, or less than 160 miles (~255 km) per month.
A Kenwood head unit with Bluetooth connectivity is the only notable modification of this car, which has some wear on the interior surfaces, creases on the seats, stains on the carpet, and some corrosion on the under-chassis surfaces. The paint chips, paint cracking next to the hood ornament, scrapes on the underside of the front bumper, and scratches on the wheels are also mentioned in the listing.
The service documentation shows that this Porsche Boxster had its engine oil and filter changed at 44,844 miles (72,169 km), in June 2024, the battery replaced at 44,290 miles (71,278 km), in October 2023, the coolant changed at 40,075 miles (64,494 km), in June 2021, and the IMS bearing replaced in February 2019, at 33,119 miles (53,300 km).
The owner reportedly bought it in February 2025, and you can find this old Porsche Boxster on Cars&Bids here , with a high bid of $700 at the time of writing. The car is advertised at no reserve, and the gavel will hit the table on December 2, 2026. How much is it worth in your opinion?
